item.title: Destroying Rigidity in the Plane
item.description: arXiv:2610.38396v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Rigidity and global rigidity are fundamental graph properties in discrete geometry, with applications to structural engineering and network localization. In two dimensions, both admit combinatorial characterizations in terms of the rigidity matroid and graph connectivity. We study the computational complexity of finding minimum-cost sets of edges or vertices whose deletion destroys either property in a finite simple graph. With unit costs, we give deterministic polynomial-time algorithms for edge deletion destroying global rigidity and vertex deletion destroying either property. We prove that edge deletion destroying rigidity is NP-hard and that, with positive integer costs, all four problems are NP-hard. These results resolve, in dimension two, the open questions on recognizing robustness under edge and vertex deletions posed by Jord\'an and Whiteley (2017), as well as the minimum edge-deletion problem for rigidity recorded in EGRES Open.
item.dc:creator: Yu Cong, Chao Xu, Yajie Zhao

item.title: Upper Bounds for CSP Non-redundancy via Locally Decodable Codes
item.description: arXiv:2610.38664v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In the study of constraint satisfaction problems (CSPs), the non-redundancy of a relation measures the maximum number of clauses in a CSP instance which can be logically independent. In the last few years, CSP non-redundancy has found a number of applications including in query complexity, sparsification, kernelization and streaming. In this paper, we present a novel technique for upper-bounding the non-redundancy of some relations using locally decodable codes (LDCs) and locally correctable codes (LCCs). More precisely, known limitations on the structure of 2-query LDCs and LCCs can be translated into limitations on the size of certain non-redundant CSP instances. This technique builds on a technique used by Brakensiek and Guruswami [STOC 2025] to bound non-redundancy via techniques from matching vector codes. Using LDCs and LCCs, we give improved upper bounds on non-redundancy of the BCK predicate pioneered by Bessiere, Carbonnel, and Katsirelos [AAAI 2020] as well as its well-studied Boolean variant. We also give the first example of a Boolean predicate whose non-redundancy is provably not of the form $n^{k\pm o(1)}$ for some positive integer $k$.
item.dc:creator: Joshua Brakensiek, David Conlon, Venkatesan Guruswami, Xiaoyu He, Jiaxi Nie, Maya Sankar, Hung-Hsun Hans Yu

item.title: Local-to-Global Theorems Based on Cones with Applications to Graph Coloring
item.description: arXiv:2610.37721v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Local-to-Global theorems are a cornerstone of many of recent developments in theoretical computer science from coding theory and PCPs all the way to analyzing mixing time of Markov chains. Building on trickledown theorems on simplicial complexes, several techniques have been established to obtain tighter local-to-global theorems to analyze the spectral gap of the Glauber dynamics, namely matrix trickledown, ${\mathcal C}$-Lorentzian polynomials and more recently Bochner type inequalities. In this paper, we adopt non-local local-to-global/Bochner type inequalities on "cones", corresponding to the local neighborhood of a given vertex, to show that the Glauber dynamics mixes in polynomial time to sample proper colorings of maximum degree $\Delta$ graphs as long as $q\geq 1.7408\Delta$.
item.dc:creator: Anqi Li, Shayan Oveis Gharan

item.title: A Characterization of Functions on the Integer Lattice That Are L-Extendable through Local Convex Extensions
item.description: arXiv:2610.38287v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: L-extendable functions on the integer lattice are functions that admit a $\frac12$UJ-convex relaxation; that is, values can be assigned to the additional half-integral points, while keeping the original values at integer points, so that the resulting function is $\frac12$UJ-convex. Various examples of L-extendable functions and their applications are known. A general characterization of L-extendability for functions on the integer lattice, however, remains open. In this paper, we study the L-extendability of functions on the integer lattice. We first obtain a necessary condition: L-extendable functions are integrally convex. We then consider a special subclass of L-extendable functions, namely, those whose local convex extensions give L-convex relaxations. This subclass has a useful optimization property: the optimal value of the original function coincides with that of the $\frac12$UJ-convex relaxation given by its local convex extension, a property not guaranteed for general $\frac12$UJ-convex relaxations. We characterize this subclass by showing that a function is L-extendable through its local convex extension if and only if it is integrally convex and its restriction to every unit hypercube is D-convex, where D-convexity is a discrete convexity associated with reflected Freudenthal simplicial divisions. This subclass strictly contains the class of D-convex functions. We also give a combinatorial characterization of D-convex subsets of the vertices of a unit hypercube: a set $X\subseteq\{0,1\}^n$ is D-convex if and only if it is majority-closed and contains a relative opposite pair.
item.dc:creator: Ken Yokoyama, Yuni Iwamasa, Kei Kimura

item.title: Moments of Magic Squares: Line-Sum Conditions, a Permutation Threshold, and Random Energies
item.description: arXiv:2610.38386v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Every semi-magic square of order $n$ satisfies the axial moment identities $\sum_{i,j}s_{ij}j^m=\sum_{i,j}s_{ij}i^m=M(n)\sum_jj^m$ for all $m\ge1$, where $M(n)=n(n^2+1)/2$. For real matrices the converse requires $1\le m\le n-1$, whereas for arrangements of $\{1,\dots,n^2\}$ fewer moments suffice once $n\ge14$. We define the permutation threshold $k^*(n)$ as the least $k$ such that every arrangement satisfying these identities for $1\le m\le k$ is semi-magic. In terms of the column-sum deviations $\gamma_j$, the degree-$k$ conditions state that $\sum_j\gamma_jt^j$ is divisible by $(t-1)^{k+1}$, linking $k^*(n)$ to the Prouhet--Tarry--Escott problem. While Schur's bound on real zeros gives $k^*(n)\le\sqrt{2(n-1)\log(n^4/4)}$, we prove the converse realisability bound $k^*(n)\ge(\sqrt2-o(1))\sqrt n$ (and $k^*(n)\ge(\sqrt6-o(1))\sqrt n$ when $4\mid n$) by perturbing semi-magic squares with complementary row pairs via horizontal swaps. We also show that $k^*(n)=n-1$ for $3\le n\le13$, $k^*(n)=n-2$ for $14\le n\le17$, and $k^*(n)\le n-3$ for $n\ge18$, and determine $k^*(n)$ for $18\le n\le40$ with computer assistance. Finally, at the $k=1$ level of the hierarchy, we specialise the Mantel--Hubert quadratic assignment variance formula to obtain exact means, variances, and limit laws under a uniform random arrangement for the full line-sum energy $E_{\mathrm{full}}$, for the four-term energy $E_4$ combining the first moments and the two diagonals, and for Loly's moment of inertia, and find that $|L_4|=14{,}639{,}440$ arrangements of order $4$ satisfy $E_4=0$.
item.dc:creator: Kyle Elliott Mathewson

item.title: Diameter-two graphs whose mutual-visibility chromatic number equals their chromatic number
item.description: arXiv:2610.39430v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A set $S$ of vertices of a graph $G$ is a mutual-visibility set if every pair of vertices of $S$ is joined by a shortest path whose internal vertices avoid $S$, and the mutual-visibility chromatic number $\chi_\mu(G)$ is the least number of mutual-visibility sets into which $V(G)$ can be partitioned. Klav\v{z}ar, Kuziak, Valenzuela Tripodoro and Yero (2025) proved that $\chi_\mu(G)\le\chi(G)$ whenever $G$ has diameter two, observed that equality holds for complete bipartite graphs, and asked whether there are any other diameter-two graphs attaining equality. We answer this question in the affirmative. We construct a graph $G_{11}$ of order 11 and diameter two with $\chi_\mu(G_{11})=\chi(G_{11})=3$, and an infinite family of such graphs obtained from $G_{11}$ by replacing one vertex with pairwise non-adjacent copies of it.
item.dc:creator: Siddhesh Chaubal

item.title: Strongly explicit Ramanujan 2-lift towers via Hilbert modular forms
item.description: arXiv:2610.39485v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Expander graphs have been central objects of study for over fifty years. Ramanujan graphs attain the asymptotically optimal nontrivial adjacency-eigenvalue threshold for infinite fixed-degree families. The original arithmetic constructions by Lubotzky-Phillips-Sarnak (1988) and Margulis (1988), and the iterative $2$-lift method of Bilu-Linial (2006) provide different approaches to Ramanujan graph constructions. Motivated by work on Mealy automata, we combine both approaches to give the following new arithmetic construction. For every prime $p\equiv 1\pmod {17}$, we construct a infinite tower of $(p+1)$-regular non-bipartite Ramanujan graphs on $2^n$ vertices, with label-preserving $2$-lifts between consecutive levels. These construction is strongly explicit: for fixed $p$, a neighbor or lift sign is computable in $O_p(n^3)$ bit operations. The construction uses fixed algebraic $2$-adic transformations, specified by finite data computable in preprocessing depending only on $p$. The main number-theoretic tool is Blasius's Ramanujan-Petersson theorem for Hilbert modular forms, applied through the Jacquet-Langlands correspondence to obtain the sharp bound $|\lambda|\leq2\sqrt p$ for every nontrivial adjacency eigenvalue of our $(p+1)$-regular graphs. The transformations preserve $2$-adic distance, which gives the binary covers and an explicit formula for their signings.
item.dc:creator: Olga Kharlampovich, Igor Pak, Alina Vdovina

item.title: Local Convergence of Triadic Closures of Sparse Random Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.39535v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Triadic closure is a natural mechanism for modeling the clustering phenomenon observed in many real-world networks. Given a possibly random undirected graph $H$, we consider pairs of non-adjacent vertices that have a common neighbor. Conditional on $H$, each such pair is joined by an edge independently and simultaneously, with a probability depending on the degrees of its endpoints and on the number of their common neighbors. The resulting graph is called a triadic closure of $H$. We study the effect of this operation on local convergence. More precisely, we prove that if a sequence of potentially random finite undirected graphs of $\left( H_n \right)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ converges locally in probability to a rooted graph $H^*$, then the corresponding sequence of triadic closures converges locally in probability to the same triadic closure of $H^*$. As a consequence, we obtain a general limit theorem for the clustering coefficients of triadic closures. In particular, we show that the triadic closures can have a strictly positive limiting clustering coefficients even when the limiting clustering coefficients of the parent graph sequence is zero. Finally, we apply our results to several classical sparse random graph models including Erd\H{o}s-R\'{e}nyi, configuration, preferential attachment models and compute the limiting clustering coefficients of their triadic closures.
item.dc:creator: Himasish Talukdar

item.title: On edge-ordered Ramsey numbers of hypergraphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.39653v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For an integer $h\geq2$, an edge-ordered $h$-uniform hypergraph $H^<$ is an $h$-uniform hypergraph with a linear ordering of its hyperedges. For an integer $q \geq 1$, the edge-ordered Ramsey number $R_{\mathrm{edge}}(H^<;q)$ of $H^<$ is the smallest positive integer $N$ such that there exists an edge-ordered $h$-uniform hypergraph $G^<$ on $N$ vertices such that, for every $q$-coloring of the hyperedges of $G^<$, there is a monochromatic copy of $H^<$ in $G^<$ preserving the hyperedge order. In this note, we show that, for every edge-ordered $h$-uniform hypergraph $F^<$ on $n$ vertices with $m\geq1$ hyperedges, $R_{\mathrm{edge}}(F^<;q) \leq R_h(F;q)^{Cm^2}$ where $F$ is the underlying unordered hypergraph, $R_h(F;q)$ is its standard $q$-color Ramsey number, and $C=C(h,q)>0$ is a constant. For fixed $h\geq3$ and $q\geq2$, this shows that prescribing the hyperedge order does not require an increase in the tower height of the classical upper bound. It also settles a problem posed by Fox and Li (2020), and for $h=2$ gives the bound $2^{O(n^4\log n)}$, improving their bounds for every fixed $q \geq 3$.
item.dc:creator: Martin Balko, Jelena Gli\v{s}i\'c

item.title: Four-Coloring Planar Graphs in Linear Time
item.description: arXiv:2610.39753v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The famous Four Color Theorem (4CT) states that any planar graph can be colored with four colors, but how do we find a 4-coloring? In our previous paper [FOCS'26], we presented a simple combinatorial algorithm to 4-color planar graphs in $O(n\log n)$ time. We improve it here to $O(n)$ time, which is optimal. The algorithm from our previous paper is based on proving that every planar triangulation has a linear number of reducible configurations or obstructing cycles. The bottleneck for the algorithm is that we need $O(\log n)$ Kempe changes to extend a recursive 4-coloring to the reducible configurations. Each Kempe change can involve a constant fraction of the graph and takes linear time. Here we show that all $O(\log n)$ Kempe changes can be identified and implemented in $O(n)$ time. The idea is to spend $O(n)$ time to preprocess the graph so that we can identify and simulate each good Kempe change in $O(n/\log n)$ amortized time. Thus, we implement all $O(\log n)$ Kempe changes in $O(n)$ total time. Based on this, we implement the whole 4-coloring in linear time. We note that creating such a representation for fast identification and simulation of the right Kempe changes is a challenge of data structures, unlike the previous paper that builds on a new graph theoretic understanding of reducible configurations.
item.dc:creator: Yuta Inoue, Ken-ichi Kawarabayashi, Atsuyuki Miyashita, Bojan Mohar, Carsten Thomassen, Mikkel Thorup

item.title: EPPA for Reducts of the Random Graph
item.description: arXiv:2610.39760v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that finite two-graphs have coherent EPPA and that neither graphs modulo global complementation nor two-graphs modulo global complementation have EPPA. This completes the classification of EPPA and coherent EPPA for the reducts of the random graph, answering a question and confirming a conjecture of Evans, Hubi\v{c}ka, Kone\v{c}n\'y and Ne\v{s}et\v{r}il.
item.dc:creator: Sofia Brenner, Jan Hubi\v{c}ka, Mat\v{e}j Kone\v{c}n\'y

item.title: Optimal self-orthogonal binary linear codes
item.description: arXiv:2610.39870v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We complete the determination of the minimum possible length of eight-dimensional binary self-orthogonal codes with given minimum distance. For dimension nine we give exact values and bounds for minimum distance at most $64$. By exploiting the geometric reformulation of linear codes as multisets of points, we fully redo the classification for dimension at most seven in a simplified and computer-free manner. As a by-product we prove the non-existence of $[93,9,44]_2$ codes and show several divisibility results for putative optimal nine-dimensional binary codes.
item.dc:creator: Sascha Kurz

item.title: Layering and reverse extension for weighted $k$-path vertex cover
item.description: arXiv:2610.40281v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the weighted $k$-path vertex cover problem for any fixed integer $k \ge 2$, in which a vertex non-negatively weighted simple graph $G = (V, E)$ is given and one wants to find a minimum-weight vertex subset $C \subseteq V$ such that every simple path on $k$ vertices in $G$ contains at least one vertex of $C$. The problem generalizes the classic weighted vertex cover problem, that is, $k = 2$, and it admits a $k$-approximation algorithm of Hochbaum~[SIAM J. Comput., 1982] and a $(k - \frac 12)$-approximation algorithm of Br\"ustle et al.~[IWOCA 2021]. In this paper, we carefully design local weight functions in the Layering and Reverse Extension local ratio framework of Bar-Yehuda et al.~[ACM Comput. Surv., 2004], leading to an approximation algorithm of ratio $\frac {3k-1}4$ for odd $k \ge 3$ and of ratio $\frac {3k}4$ for even $k \ge 4$. When $k = 3$ and $k = 4$, these ratios are $2$ and $3$, respectively, matching the state-of-the-art approximation ratios for the corresponding special cases.
item.dc:creator: Jiajing Wu, An Zhang, Shiming Li, Guohui Lin

item.title: Half-Optimal Induced Matchings in Random Graphs: Online and Low-Degree Algorithms
item.description: arXiv:2610.40369v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For many optimization problems on random graphs, most prominently the largest independent set problem, natural algorithms reach only half the optimum, and such factor-two gaps are known to be sharp within broad algorithmic classes. We prove such a gap for finding large induced matchings in Erd\H{o}s-R\'enyi random graphs. In the worst case, requiring a matching to be induced turns a polynomial-time solvable problem into an NP-hard one; our results reveal an average-case counterpart. In $G(n,p)$ with $C/n\le p\le 1-\kappa$, the largest induced matching has size $(1+o(1))L$ with high probability, where $L=\log_{1/(1-p)}(np)$. A simple online greedy algorithm finds an induced matching of size $(1/2-\epsilon)L$, while no online algorithm, even with adaptive inspection order and unbounded computation, finds one of size $(1/2+\epsilon)L$ except with probability $\exp(-\Omega(L\log(np)))$. In the sparse regime $p=d/n$, low-degree polynomial algorithms exhibit the same sharp threshold. Our guarantees rest on a maximality principle: with high probability, every maximal induced matching is half-optimal. Greedy outputs a maximal induced matching and our low-degree algorithm a near-maximal one. We bypass the delicate coupling arguments classically used to analyze greedy since Karp. For low-degree hardness, we adapt Wein's overlap gap argument, with forbidden structures that track overlaps between endpoint sets rather than edge sets, since a new edge may join two previously used endpoints and thus encounter no fresh randomness. For online hardness, we give a new and significantly simpler argument that avoids the correlated instances of prior OGP-based proofs: at a suitable stopping time, all pairs involving uninspected vertices remain unrevealed, so a direct first-moment bound suffices.
item.dc:creator: Abhishek Dhawan, Eren C. K{\i}z{\i}lda\u{g}, Neeladri Maitra, Cheng Mao, Timothy L. H. Wee

item.title: Average pairwise Hamming distance of a subset in a hypercube
item.description: arXiv:2610.40486v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this note, we prove that for a subset $\mathcal{F}$ of $\{0,1\}^n$ of density $\frac{1}{8}$, its average pairwise Hamming distance is at least $\frac{n-3}{2}$, with equality attained only by $(n-3)$-dimensional subcubes. This answers a question of Lei Yu, and solves an important open case of a more general question posed by Ahlswede and Katona in 1977.
item.dc:creator: Yijia Fang, Hao Huang

item.title: Tight Lower Bound for Multicolor Discrepancy
item.description: arXiv:2504.18489v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove the following asymptotically tight lower bound for $k$-color discrepancy: For any $k \geq 2$, there exists a hypergraph with $n$ hyperedges such that its $k$-color discrepancy is at least $\Omega(\sqrt{n})$. This improves on the previously known lower bound of $\Omega(\sqrt{n/\log k})$ due to Caragiannis et al. (arXiv:2502.10516). As an application, we show that our result implies improved lower bounds for group fair division.
item.dc:creator: Pasin Manurangsi, Raghu Meka

item.title: Fractional Iterates and Oscillatory Convergence
item.description: arXiv:2510.25606v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The simple continued fractions for the Golden & Silver means are well-known. It is astonishing that, as far as we know, no one has published half-iterates (let alone quarter-iterates) for the corresponding algorithms. We also examine the cosine and logistic maps (with parameter $2 < \lambda < 3$).
item.dc:creator: Steven Finch

item.title: Magic Gems: Convex Hulls of Lifted Magic Squares
item.description: arXiv:2512.09170v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Given an arrangement of $\{1,\dots,n^2\}$ in an $n\times n$ grid, we lift each cell to $\mathbb{R}^3$ by centring its grid coordinates $(x,y)$ at the origin and taking its centred entry $z = s_{ij} - (n^2+1)/2$ as a vertical height. The convex hull of these $n^2$ points is the gem of the arrangement, whose lower and upper boundaries are the regular subdivisions of the grid induced by $\pm z$. While random arrangements and generic linear magic squares have gems whose vertex counts grow with $n$, our main theorem shows that the classical Siamese (de la Loub\`ere) magic square of every odd order $n\ge5$ has $f$-vector $(12,26,16)$, isometry group $\{\pm\mathrm{id}\}$, and only the twelve vertices forced by the boundary of the grid. The proof shears the lift onto five horizontal terraces and reduces the hull calculation to a finite table of polynomials in $m=(n-1)/2$; the same method gives $f$-vector $(12,24,14)$ for the base-$n$ digit-exchanged square. Along any family of linear squares with fixed steps the $f$-vector is eventually periodic in $n$, whereas over all linear magic squares of prime order $n$ the maximum vertex count grows as $\Theta(\ln n)$. Whenever the heights have vanishing first moments, a short principal-axes argument shows that the point set has a non-trivial isometry if and only if the arrangement is self-complementary up to dihedral symmetry. An exact census of the $880$ magic squares of order four yields $616$ congruence classes and $352$ combinatorial types of gems, and shows that while vertex and facet counts are nearly insensitive to the magic line-sum conditions, the volume and solid centroid shift systematically.
item.dc:creator: Kyle Elliott Mathewson

item.title: Coloring t-perfect graphs with fewer colors
item.description: arXiv:2607.05961v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Recently, Chudnovsky, Cook, Davies, Oum, and Tan obtained the first finite bound on the chromatic number of t-perfect graphs, showing that they are 199053-colorable. We improve this bound to 130 by refining their proof. The original proof establishes that every graph with large odd girth and large chromatic number contains a certain structure called an r-arithmetic rope, and that its existence in a certain leveling of a graph with large odd girth would imply an odd wheel as a t-minor, a known obstruction to t-perfectness. While their technique requires a lower bound on the chromatic number that is exponential in r, we show that the existence of an r-arithmetic rope can already be guaranteed under a linear bound. Using a slightly weakened notion of arithmetic ropes allows us to reduce the bound even further.
item.dc:creator: Matija Novakovi\'c, Stefan Weltge

item.title: The list size of random linear and LDPC codes at capacity
item.description: arXiv:2609.06570v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We show that for every prime power $q$ and $\rho\in(0,1-\frac1q)$ there exists $\varepsilon_0(q, \rho) > 0$ such that for all positive $\varepsilon < \varepsilon_0(q, \rho)$, a random linear code over $\mathbb{F}_q$ of rate $1-h_q(\rho)-\varepsilon$ has list size $\lfloor h_q(\rho)/\varepsilon\rfloor$ or $\lfloor h_q(\rho)/\varepsilon\rfloor+1$ with probability $1-o(1)$. Before this work, the list size was known only up to a constant factor for $q\ge3$, and for $q=2$ it was known to be either $\lfloor h_2(\rho)/\varepsilon\rfloor-1$, $\lfloor h_2(\rho)/\varepsilon\rfloor$ or $\lfloor h_2(\rho)/\varepsilon\rfloor+1$. We also show that the same two-point concentration holds for the list size of random LDPC codes. This follows from a general theorem establishing that random LDPC codes and random linear codes have the same threshold rate for distance, list decoding, list recovery from errors and any other \emph{convex} property, which answers a question of Mosheiff, Resch, Ron-Zewi, Silas and Wootters.
item.dc:creator: Shashwat Silas

item.title: Arc Kayles is PSPACE-complete
item.description: arXiv:2609.23777v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We show that Arc Kayles is PSPACE-complete. This solves a question raised by Schaefer in 1976.
item.dc:creator: \'Edouard Bonnet

item.title: Breaking the Infinite Barrier in the $\frac{1}{3}$--$\frac{2}{3}$ Conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2609.30888v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The balance constant is a poset parameter measuring how well random linear extensions can be split according to their relative order on two elements. We give an $\varepsilon$-improvement for the balance constant over the bound by Brightwell, Felsner and Trotter (1995), for some small $\varepsilon>0$. This is the first general result towards the $\frac{1}{3}$--$\frac{2}{3}$ conjecture in over 30 years.
item.dc:creator: Max Aires, Swee Hong Chan, Igor Pak, Greta Panova

item.title: Identifying codes of Archimedean grids
item.description: arXiv:2610.32192v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: An identifying code of a graph is a dominating set $C$ such that the sets $N[v]\cap C$ are pairwise distinct. The minimum density of an identifying code has been studied extensively for several infinite grids. It is known to be $1/4$ for the triangular grid and $7/20$ for the square grid, whereas for the hexagonal grid the problem is still open, between $5/12$ and $53/126$. These three grids are the regular members of the family of the eleven Archimedean grids. In this paper, we start a systematic study of identifying codes in this family. We determine the minimum density for five of the nine Archimedean grids for which it was not known: it is $2/3$ for the truncated hexagonal grid, $3/7$ for the truncated square grid, and $1/3$ for the trihexagonal (kagome) grid, the elongated triangular grid and the snub hexagonal grid. All lower bounds are proved by the discharging method. For the three remaining non-regular Archimedean grids, we also obtain some bounds: the minimum density lies between $3/7$ and $13/30$ for the truncated trihexagonal grid, between $1/3$ and $11/30$ for the rhombitrihexagonal grid, and between $2/7$ and $9/28$ for the snub square grid. As a by-product, we prove that every identifying code of a cubic graph with the slow growth property in which every vertex lies on exactly one triangle (resp. $4$-cycle) has density at least $2/3$ (resp. $3/7$).
item.dc:creator: Rudini Sampaio
